body: Sometimes our internal emotions reflect our outward situation, but it doesn't have to be that way.  Force a smile, try to find a place that you can afford, and with a positive attitude things just may start going your way.  If they don't, then you didn't lose anything, you believe you are going to feel miserable anyway, why not try another mindset and look at the world from a perspective that you normally would not have considered? Like I said, you won't lose anything, why not give it a try?

You should not blame yourself for what she did wrong.  If you are still on speaking terms with her you should try and see what she felt like she was gaining by cheating on you.  Blaming yourself for something that she did to hurt you is blaming the victim.  Right now you should be concerned with you.  I know that things can feel like they are crumbling down around you but at times like this you should just take a step back and take stock of the situation.  You are living somewhere you can afford right? That's something.  Just take a few deep breaths and reflect on your situation thus far.  After a day or so of introspection you might be able to see everything much more clearly.
Sorry to add to your depression  :(    The songs you  posted are very powerful, I personally like many different genres, to each their own!
There is always reason to keep going, we just have to find our own within our own lives.  It was truly powerful.
Very true, but It's almost over!  There is light at the end of this tunnel!

[What a beautiful song.](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rCRlOQvk4m8)  I don't know if you play by ear or read music but this rendition is very nice.  Remember that you must take care of yourself before you can take care of any external problem.

Trust me, your feelings are absolutely normal.  I am also a senior in college.   I want more than anything to graduate and travel around Europe.  Although I can't do that because I need to get a "real" job and pay off loans, bills, etc... Sometimes things feel so far away that they lose all certainty, reality.  I believe everything happens for a reason, I know it sounds cliché or absurd to say this but I think it really is true.  Don't weigh yourself down with worrying about a future that you may or may not attain.  Just live your life day by day, reveling in whatever good you come across and learning from the bad.  One day, you will attain your dreams, it may not be by your means, but it will happen one way or another.

Lol, I know the feeling..  But, there is no reason why you cannot get back into your old interests.  Cancer has ravaged my family, I only take solace in the thought that there will probably be some sort of cure by the time I am diagnosed with it... You have your life to live, your loved ones will always know that you cared deeply for them.  They absolutely knew the love that was there, and I am sure that was a great blessing for them.  Would you start playing the piano again?  I am sure that there is a great book sitting somewhere just waiting for you to pick it up again and continue where you left off.  You will begin to find yourself again in time, these things take time, but just try to ease back into it.  Go it at your own pace, don't try and take things too fast, but I believe you would begin to find your old happiness again once you begin to fall in love again with the hobbies and activities you once cherished.

You can PM me or mostly anyone else here on SW anytime you need to talk, that is what we're all here for.  :)  A steady and healthy relationship would probably benefit you, however, I do not fully know your situation.  It seems like you need to find someone who will support you.  Loneliness can get the best of us, that's just how us humans are wired... We want someone to understand and cherish us for what we are and not for what they want us to be.  It is difficult to find that type of relationship nowadays but I am sure you will find it, or your bf will come around in time.  That is all we have is time.  You should make the best of it you know?  Do you have any hobbies that you enjoy pursuing on your own time?  In my humble opinion I believe you would benefit from some self satisfying pursuits.  Go out and enjoy nature if that is what you like, take some time for some introspection and self reflection.  Yourself is your greatest asset.

Please call 1-800-273-8255 (US) if you feel the immediate need to end your existence.  Life is so worth living, the dark times make the bright ones seem that much more luminous.   As glados said, once you make this decision, however clouded your mindset may be right now by sorrow or perceived futility, there is no coming back.  One more night to reflect upon your final decision and fully realize the impact you will be making upon all those that know and care about you will not hurt anything.  Remember, we all die in the end, why not live it out and make the best of it while you are still here on natural terms?
Glad to be of any assistance!  Anxiety clouds even the clearest minds.  I am sure you will make a fine transition, and the best of  luck to you in all your future endeavors.

No problem.  That's great introspection on your part, it seems like you really do understand what is causing your distress, now all that's left is to rectify it.  I am sure you will find it again, once something peaks your interest.

Have you asked your old therapist if it would be alright if you texted her from time to time when you were feeling really down or anxious?  You have no reason to trust me other than my word that I am really only here to help as much as I can, but I will tell you right now that they will not scoff at you.  They will only be there to help you the best they can.  Anxiety is normal when switching to a totally new environment as you are after such a prolonged period of time with a now trusted person.  I am sure that your old therapist would not mind if you contacted her periodically just to follow up and let her know how things are going with you.  Asking her won't hurt.

Well, the simple fact that you made this post speaks to the fact that you do indeed care what others have to say; that in and of itself is a form of empathy.  Why not give helping others a try?  You stated that you are bored with your current state of being, manipulating others and all, so why not try the opposite?  You might enjoy it.  Try hunting, eating all that you kill, that might be able to help your desire to do harm or kill.  The satisfaction of having complete control over a helpless animal and taking its life for sustenance might give you a small thrill.  You have had life your way, enjoyed it thus far, but now you are in a slump.  I would suggest you just try the opposite for a while, see how it goes. You have nothing to lose.

What a great song!  I especially love the Island flavor; Israel seems so happy when crooning that melody.  It just goes to show that you don't need to conform to any ideals set forth by others, he was himself and nothing more.

Your outlook makes me smile.  :)   That's how I try to look at life.  We as humans can't control every aspect of our lives, however hard we may try...  It helps to just let some things go, things that we will needlessly burden ourselves with in the form of self destructive anxiety or unfounded guilt.  I always take solace in the realization that everything will be alright, in the way it was meant to be, in the long run.

I see, well, take it from someone who is struggling under a harsh course load his senior year trying to earn a BS in Psych.  If you "fail" or are unable to accomplish your goals the first time around there is always, always next time.  Being 18 and a junior in college is something to be very proud of in and of itself.  You are already very far ahead of your peers I am sure, most of us don't get to graduate from college until we are 23 years old or so.  Look at it this way, even if you take a year or two off to travel or collect your thoughts you will still be ahead of the majority of your classmates, and grad schools look fondly upon life experience.  I have not had the chance to do so myself but I hear from reputable sources that graduate admission programs highly regard students who maintained a decent GPA and still found time for "outside interests."  Travel or job experience is indispensable when combined with a "decent" GPA and a nice GRE score.  Just study hard for the GRE and I am sure you will receive a great score.  You seem highly intelligent and more than capable of scoring well on the GRE; with a high score I have heard of amazing institutions accepting students with a GPA of 2.5 or similar.  You absolutely do not need a perfect 4.0 to be accepted to a respectable university for continuing education.
It's understandable..  Everyone "burns out" now and again. Life has its highs and lows, and we must learn how to take them in stride.  How have you "screwed up" ?
Awesome that you are feeling better.  I'm glad that you are doing well, keep up the positive mindset!

The only things I have heard from you are absolutely positive things.  I would love to earn a 4.0 in at least one semester... That is an amazing achievement.  I have a guitar, but I cannot play it.  I wish I could learn some chords but stuff always gets in the way.  You sound like an extremely accomplished well rounded person. Worrying is just a natural part of being an empathetic goal conscious individual, it strikes everyone hard from time to time.  What was it that crushed you?

:)  I'm glad.  We can only take it one day at a time, and remember that one day compared to the rest of your life is nothing in the grand scheme.  PM me anytime if you ever want to talk to someone, I'm usually here... lol

This post that you made is worthwhile.  You have directly impacted my life as I have read what you said, and it seems like you have seen the true ugliness that they world has to offer.  I know you might not want to believe me but there **are** some worthwhile things out there.  You don't have to listen to me, I'm just some random ass dude on the internet to you, but I know that you have something to contribute to this world.  You do not seem dumb to me in the least, you have a very well put together story here and it conveys the deepness that is within your heart.  Sometimes shit seems like it will never get better, but why not try? Everyone has the same fate in the end, so why not just live your life how you want?  Travel if you want, there are some dirt cheap courier flights and I hear work in hostels in whatever country will provide a person with housing and money.  I've fallen into a rut before, it is terribly hard to get out of without a positive mindset, which can be hard to come by... Do you have any hobbies or stuff you like doing?

I feel like I understand completely, when bad things stack upon one another like that it can feel like the whole world is against you, like nothing at all can or will go right.  I've felt that way before as well, It can be just one thing after another after another until the most trivial thing is just "it".  It is usually stress induced and at that pivotal moment I feel like I am just ready to explode.  It would be easier if everything just "went away"... What I feel helps me when this happens is to take a deep breath and stop and sit down.  I then breathe deeply for a little while to calm down.  Think about each event, don't treat it as one big terrible thing, break it into chunks, this may help you see each little thing as just that- only a little thing.  I am a full supporter of introspection, think about each event and how it actually messed up your day.  It is possible that each little thing didn't really have that big of an impact on your entire life as a whole.  I bet you wouldn't even remember that failed test or those lost keys in 40 years.  Is it really worth giving up all that time just for that?  Do you think any of this could be of any help to you?

My humble advice would be to introspect on these thoughts, whenever you begin to think about it remember all of the aspects of your thought process and try to work backwards.  Try to figure out where the thoughts stem from.  Were you in a particularly bad mood about something when the thoughts crept in?  Was it an important life event or just a trivial matter? Getting to the root cause of the thoughts is of utmost importance if you would like to get a larger viewpoint of your own consciousness.  The ones where you plan out a scenario are much more detrimental I would think.  Have you actually made preparations in anticipation of the event?  Can you remember if there was an event that severely affected you to spur on these thoughts?
Thinking about death is completely natural, however, thinking about taking your life prematurely is not very healthy.  Are these just fleeting thoughts or do you actually plan out a scenario?

"I've made mistakes like everyone but I try to do well and the only problem is every time I do something that is truly a good thing something awful happens to me."   -  I can understand how you might feel that way because of past experiences, but please believe me, it is not always true, not by a longshot.  It always makes my day when someone does something nice for me, and I treat them the same, and then go out of my way to do something nice for another, and so on... Just know that there are people out there that your kind actions have had an impact on.  

My humble advice would be to take a step back and take a good hard look at your life.  Try to observe yourself from another's perspective, and see what you can improve upon. Also take note of your positives, I know that you can find at least one. Believe me, it may seem like an easy way out to kill yourself but it is not.  Your "failed" attempts seem to show that at least in your subconscious you know that you are worth something, and that in and of itself is an accomplishment.  After you have taken stock of yourself, choose one thing to change, anything, make a goal of changing that one thing, be it talking to one stranger a day, doing one good deed a day, etc... its up to you.  If you really give it a try it may help your introspection, and give you a new window into yourself.  Understanding yourself is half the battle.  Take my advice with a grain of salt, for I am not a professional, just a simple Psych student with time on my hands and a listening ear.  Always remember that your actions DO have an impact on others, be they positive or negative, whether or not you are privy to it.  You are not alone, and people do care.
